I wanted to point out a small error in the titling of this article and subsequent submission on Voat.

The title of the article reads as follows:

Obama Allows Immigrants to Skip Oath of Allegiance to America and Pledge to Defend America

This is not entirely accurate. Yes, according to the information provided in the article, immigrants can opt-out of pledging to, "bear arms on behalf of the United States," as is stated in the article:

Immigrants seeking to become citizens no longer have to pledge to â€œbear arms on behalf of the United States.â€ They can opt out of that part of the Oath.

That and they do not have to, "cite any specific religious belief that forbids them to perform military service."

However, this is just about all they can opt-out of. Yes, I do agree that it's insane that immigrants can opt-out of any part of the Oath of Allegiance. They should have to swear full loyalty to the country they wish to come over to; however, the title states (just as the original Breitbart article does) that they can opt-out of the Oath entirely, which is not true.

Something else interesting to note, as it's mentioned in the Breitbart article, the USCIS can change the Oath of Allegiance at any time without approval of Congress:

But the fact is, unelected bureaucrats at the USCIS can change the wording of the Oath without approval of the peopleâ€™s representatives in Congress.

So, the change is not actually illegal, however unethical and dirty a practice it is.

Just wanted to point that out for clarification.

TL;DR: The title is incorrect. Immigrants cannot skip the entire oath, only certain parts. It's still bad that this has happened, but it's actually not illegal.

It's all about the daily irradiance values which explains why the Earth's tilt from the sun causes these temperature swings. Irradiance is simply the amount of energy from sunlight per square meter that hits the Earth's surface. With a greater tilt away from the sun, we receive less irradiance which causes winter; with a greater tilt towards the sun, we receive more irradiance which causes the summer (this is only true for the northern hemisphere. For the southern hemisphere, the opposite is true.)

The northern hemisphere gets almost twice the energy in the summer months compared to the winter months, but only at my specific location where I'm at. It'll vary depending on the latitude, and, I believe, your altitude as well. It's all pretty much geometry and understanding the quantity of light that strikes the Earth's surface at different angles.

You seem to understand the distances and orbital dynamics, so skip this if you don't need an explanation as to how this part works. Anyways, there are two major factors in how our seasons change. The first is the way that orbital dynamics work - Orbital bodies don't actually go in a circle around the thing they're orbiting, they make an elongated shape that looks more like this () as a consequence of the way gravity works. (Imagine the sun as creating a gigantic valley around it, and the Earth effectively rolls down the hill at the Sun, except it wasn't pointed directly at it. It zips by and starts rolling up the other side of the hill, eventually slows down and comes to a stop, and then rolls back down the slope towards the sun, zipping passed it again. Reality is a little more complicated than this, but it'll do for the purposes of this explanation.) As a consequence of us being at different relative distances from the Sun, the amount of Solar Radiation that we're exposed to on the side that's facing the sun increases or decreases. Naturally, the side that's tilted closer to the sun has longer exposure at a more direct angle of incident (Meaning more radiation density) so that area gets hotter.

Now, continuing along to "how do we not get scorched to oblivion" is where our atmosphere comes in. Basically, in very simple terms it works like boiling water - Water takes a lot of energy to heat up, and it transfers that energy extremely efficiently from areas of high concentration to areas of lower concentration. As an example, if you pour cold water on a pan that was boiling hot, within moments it's cool enough to touch. Now, take that effect and multiply it by an average of two tons of atmosphere sitting on top of you, and a global water system - It takes a lot to heat that up, and the fact that the heat will move from areas of high concentration to areas of lower concentration mean that the average temperature can stay within habitable range on the scope of the planet. Long story short, the energy disperses relatively efficiently over a large area, and living things harness that energy to power their metabolic functions. Basically, the Earth is really, really good at storing energy from solar radiation because of the atmosphere, and changes to the seasons are consequently caused by the differential in saturation by solar radiation to specific parts of the atmosphere, which need to disperse heat into areas that are comparatively cooler.

TL;DR: Earth's Atmosphere absorbs a ridiculous amount of the solar radiation, so the amount of relative exposure it gets matters a lot, so the tilt and point in orbit change everything.
